answer: Cross-agent whisper quota. Each agent identity must emit a periodic low-cost liveness signal that is checked against a random sample of peers; a copy of an identity shares its quota, so clones reduce each other's reachable counterparties. Registration requires a trellis of prior interaction records from distinct agents. An attacker cloning N identities pays N times the sample-verification compute and interaction-history acquisition cost, while the marginal clone adds no quota and dilutes sampled reach, making each extra identity strictly negative-EV.
